coveragePlanContract: Every category and foodGroup below exists in coverage-plan.<coveragePlanVersion>.json, and each entry's category equals that foodGroup's own category there. That agreement holds by construction: the entries were emitted by a generator that refused to write the file on any mismatch, unknown category, unknown foodGroup or unknown foodState. scripts/lib/manifest.ts enforces only the version field at load time (loadUsdaManifest checks usdaManifestVersion against EXPECTED_USDA_MANIFEST_VERSION and throws ManifestError, which catalog-import-usda.ts preflight reports as the usda_manifest_unavailable gap); it passes no structural check for this document. Re-asserting the cross-file agreement against the loaded coverage plan therefore belongs to the importer, and a mismatch must stop the run before the first USDA request rather than halfway through an import.
usdaDataTypeEncoding: Percent-encode dataType values (Survey%20(FNDDS)). URLSearchParams encodes a space as '+' and USDA answers 400 for 'Survey (FNDDS)' when it does.
brandedDataTypePolicy: 'Branded' is listed because the USDA API accepts it and the running API's branded search uses it, but no datasetSweep enumerates it and no entry below selects it: manufacturer records enter the catalog only through a curated entry, never through a bulk import. USDA FoodData Central is public domain with no retention restrictions (recorded in src/services/usda.service.ts and on the usda_api_cache model), which is what makes committing the identity data in this file and snapshotting per-100 g values into a release legal; no other provider's data appears here.
sourceKeyContract: catalog_foods.source_key is UNIQUE and is the key every import upserts on, so rerunning this manifest updates in place instead of inserting duplicates; catalog_foods.usda_fdc_id is UNIQUE too, so two entries may never name the same fdcId. Recipe seeds and search-benchmark expectations reference foods by this string and never by a database id, which is what lets a release load into any database.
entryIdentityContract: Each foods entry carries exactly one of fdcId (an integer read from a live USDA response) or resolveBy, the shape scripts/lib/manifest.ts declares as UsdaFoodResolveBy {query, dataTypes?, requireDescription?}: a lookup the importer performs once, pins and reports, where requireDescription is the exact description the resolved record must carry. Never both fields, and never a guessed id, because a fabricated FDC id imports the wrong food under a name that looks right. Every entry in this version carries a verified fdcId, so resolveBy is unused here; the importer must still support it, because a later append may name a food whose id cannot be verified at authoring time.
expectedUsdaDescriptionContract: expectedUsdaDescription is the description the record carried when its id was verified. The importer compares it with the live record and, on a mismatch, records identity_status "ambiguous" and reports the entry instead of trusting the id, so an upstream re-identification surfaces as a review item rather than a silently wrong food.

importLimits.rateLimitHeadroomReason: Leaves 100 requests an hour on the same key for the running API's estimate, label-scan and branded-search traffic.
importLimits.limiterNote: fetchFromUsda retries 400 alongside 429 and 5xx because USDA intermittently rejects requests that succeed when retried verbatim, so one logical call can cost up to four tokens. The limiter therefore counts physical attempts, and pauses when the bucket empties instead of failing the run.

nutrientShapes.searchResults: foodNutrients in /foods/search and /foods results are per 100 g (or per 100 ml), for every generic data type.
nutrientShapes.detailLabelNutrients: labelNutrients in /food/{fdcId}?format=full are already per serving, and its keys are protein, carbohydrates (not carbs), fat and calories. The two shapes must never be mixed: this import reads the per-100 g foodNutrients and takes gram weights from foodPortions.

portionResolution.selectorNotWeight: defaultPortion names a portion; it never carries a gram weight. The importer reads it from the gram weight on the record's own foodPortions entry, and an entry whose selector resolves to nothing is quarantined with check "missing_gram_weight" rather than published, because an invented gram weight is a fabricated number.
portionResolution.labelByDataset: The portion label is `modifier` for SR Legacy; `measureUnit` plus any `portionDescription` qualifier, joined with a comma, for Foundation; and `portionDescription` for Survey (FNDDS), where the amount is embedded at the start of the string and must be parsed off first — an FNDDS `modifier` is a numeric measure code and is never a label. For SR Legacy and Foundation the amount is the separate `amount` field.
portionResolution.selectorFields: defaultPortion carries the label in the field the record's own dataset uses, matching UsdaDefaultPortionSelector in scripts/lib/manifest.ts: `modifier` for SR Legacy and `portionDescription` for Survey (FNDDS) and Foundation. Exactly one of the two is present on every entry, so the importer reads the field for the dataset it is already dispatching on and never has to guess which one carries the label.
portionResolution.matching: Consider only portions whose amount equals defaultPortion.amount and whose gram weight is greater than zero. Prefer a portion whose label equals the selector label (modifier or portionDescription) after case-insensitive whitespace normalization; fall back to portions whose label contains it. Where more than one remains, the lowest gram weight wins, so resolution is deterministic. Equality is preferred because a containment-only rule resolves "medium" against both a medium carrot and a medium carrot slice, and the amount must be compared separately because SR Legacy keeps it in its own `amount` field rather than in the label.
portionResolution.verified: Every amount and label pair below resolved against the live record when its fdcId was verified: 143 of the 145 entries resolve to exactly one gram weight, and the two that remain multi-valued (potato chips at 28 and 28.35 g for "oz", granola bar at 21 and 25 g for "bar") are two genuine USDA rows for the same label, where the lowest-weight rule decides.

sweepClassificationRules.matching: Each rule carries exactly one of descriptionStartsWith or descriptionContains, and matches when any of its strings matches. Rules are evaluated in array order and the first match wins, so order is load-bearing: composite-dish rules precede ingredient rules because an as-eaten description names its ingredients, spice rules precede produce rules so "spices, onion powder" is not an onion, oil and plant-milk rules precede nut and dairy rules so "oil, coconut" is not a coconut, and snack rules precede produce rules so "snacks, potato chips" is not a potato.
sweepClassificationRules.deterministic: Classification is a pure function of the description and this table. No model call is made anywhere in this import, and no rule consults nutrition values.

fallback.reason: A record that matches no rule is imported as a candidate and left unpublished pending a curator, rather than being published under a guessed category. Publishing an unclassified food would put it in the wrong grocery aisle and make it invisible to the dislike exclusions.

sweepClassificationRules.appendOnlyContract: Rules are appended, never reordered or edited. The first-match-wins evaluation order therefore guarantees that an appended rule can only classify a description no earlier rule matched, so adding rules can raise coverage but can never change an existing classification. Rules carrying appendedBy were added after the first 127 were reviewed, and their block records which pass added them.
sweepClassificationRules.excludeFromPublicationContract: A rule may carry excludeFromPublication: true. It means the description was recognised and is deliberately outside this catalog's scope - restaurant and fast-food menu items, and infant, toddler and baby foods - rather than unclassified. The importer skips such a record entirely: no catalog_foods row is written, and the skip is counted under skippedExcludedClass so the report shows how many records were recognised-and-declined rather than silently dropped. Restaurant items are branded identities (brandedDataTypePolicy), and infant nutrition is out of the feature's scope.

sweepFoodStateRules.fallbackReason: Survey (FNDDS) descriptions are as-eaten, so an unmatched FNDDS record is prepared; the reference datasets describe the food as bought, so an unmatched record there is as_purchased. The state is never guessed from nutrition, and raw, dry and cooked forms stay separate rows because grocery aggregation keys on (catalog_food_id, food_state) and must never merge them.

sweepAliasPolicy: A swept record's aliases are derived from its own description only: the comma-separated qualifiers reordered into natural order ("Rice, brown, long-grain, raw" yields "brown rice"), plus the plural of the head noun. The sweep invents no synonym, regional name or misspelling — those are curation decisions and exist only on the foods entries above.
sweepPageBounds: Each sweep's observedLastNonEmptyPage and observedApproximateRecordCount were measured against GET /foods/list at pageSize 200 on observedOn, by binary-searching the last page that still returned a non-empty array. maxPages is a backstop bound and not that measurement: it sits above the observed count so a dataset that grows between authoring and import is not silently truncated, while an enumeration that never returns an empty page still terminates. The real stopping conditions are an empty page and stopWhenCategoryCandidateVolumeReached; maxPages only caps a runaway.

genericDatasetVolume.consequence: The three generic datasets hold about 13,619 records in total, which is below the coverage plan's candidateVolumeTotal, so this import cannot by itself reach the candidate volume however completely it sweeps — and a per-category ceiling binds sooner still, because these records are not distributed the way the plan's categories are. The gap is what catalog-generate-ai.ts fills (aiCandidates = max(0, candidateVolume - usdaCandidates) per category), and any remaining shortfall is reported exactly by catalog-report.ts rather than padded. Recorded as a measurement so the arithmetic downstream starts from an observed number instead of an assumed one.

datasetSweeps.note: Foundation records are the newest analytically measured reference foods and are swept first so that, where the same food exists in both, the Foundation measurement is the one already present when the SR Legacy sweep reaches it.
SR Legacy is the bulk of the single-ingredient coverage and the richest source of household portions, which is why most curated entries above resolve to it.
Survey (FNDDS) supplies the as-eaten preparations and composite dishes that the prepared_meal category needs and that the reference datasets do not carry.

workListOrder: The importer walks foods in array order and then datasetSweeps in array order, checkpointing by index across both sections, so entries are only ever appended and never reordered or removed: reordering would make an interrupted run resume at the wrong food. skipFdcIdsPresentInFoods keeps a sweep from overwriting a curated entry, so curation always wins over pattern classification.

sweepBrandExclusionRules.appliesTo: the USDA description as written, before lower-casing
sweepBrandExclusionRules.purpose: Enforces brandedDataTypePolicy on the sweeps: a manufacturer or product identity enters the catalog only through a curated foods entry, never through a bulk import. A swept record matching any signal below is skipped - no catalog_foods row - and counted under skippedBrandPattern.
sweepBrandExclusionRules.whyNotFindBrandPatternMatch: src/services/catalog.logic.ts exports findBrandPatternMatch, but its own contract scopes it to AI-generated candidates, where it is a reject-tier check. Its proper-noun heuristic false-positives on USDA's own comma-inverted descriptions - "Beef, New Zealand, imported, chuck eye roll" reads as a proper noun followed by a product form - so the sweeps use the three precise signals below and findBrandPatternMatch stays what it says it is.

allCapsRun.rule: A whitespace-delimited token of three or more letters that is entirely upper-case and is not in allowedAllCaps. USDA writes manufacturer names in upper case in its own descriptions, so an unexplained all-caps token is the single most reliable brand signal in this corpus.

sweepBrandExclusionRules.measuredOutcome: 719 of 12,177 classified generic records flagged (549 by allCapsRun, 170 by brandWordContains), leaving 11,458 for the detail pass.
sweepBrandExclusionRules.curatedEntriesExempt: foods entries are never screened: their identity was reviewed by hand and their fdcId verified against a live response.

sweepCostClassRules.purpose: A swept record has no curated costClass, and cost_class is NOT NULL. These are relative-cost policy per coverage category, on the coverage plan's 1-3 costClassScale: 1 inexpensive staple, 2 moderately priced, 3 premium or specialty. The value feeds recipe budget tiers only (AAP 0.7.3); it is never shown to a user and is never a price.
sweepCostClassRules.matching: The record's classified category. Every one of the 21 categories has a row, so the rule is total.
sweepCostClassRules.foodGroupOverridesFirst: A foodGroup listed in foodGroupOverrides wins over its category's default.

sweepAllergenDietRules.purpose: A swept record carries no curated allergen or diet review, so these rules derive allergen_tags and diet_tags from its classified food group and its own description. The derivation only ever narrows: it can add an allergen and it can remove a diet tag, never the reverse.
sweepAllergenDietRules.allergenStatusRule: allergen_status is 'unknown' for every swept record without exception. A single-ingredient reference food's allergens are inferable, but inference is not review, and allergen_status is the column the planner reads to decide whether a food is safe to put in front of someone with an allergy (AAP 0.7.3 requires allergen_status = 'known' for every planned ingredient). Recording 'unknown' means a swept food publishes - resolveCatalogDisposition publishes a usda-source record carrying the review-tier allergens_unknown flag - is searchable in Add Food, and is excluded from recipe eligibility until a curator reviews it. The 145 curated entries are the reviewed set and keep allergen_status 'known'.

dietDerivation.hierarchy: vegan implies vegetarian implies pescatarian_ok, matching the 139 reviewed rows, where every vegan food also carries vegetarian and pescatarian_ok. gluten_free is orthogonal.
dietDerivation.rule: Start from all four tags. Remove vegan, vegetarian and pescatarian_ok when the category is an animalCategory other than protein_seafood, or an animalMarker appears. Remove vegan, vegetarian and keep pescatarian_ok when only a seafoodMarker appears or the category is protein_seafood. Remove vegan but keep vegetarian and pescatarian_ok when a dairyEggMarker appears. Remove gluten_free when a wheat allergen was derived. Honey removes vegan only.

compositeMarkers.purpose: A description naming a composite preparation has ingredients its food group does not predict, so its derived allergen set is a floor rather than a set. Recorded in the validation record's nutrition_assumptions so a curator can see why review is still required.

sweepNamingPolicy.canonicalName: The USDA description, lower-cased and whitespace-normalised, verbatim otherwise. USDA descriptions are comma-inverted and highly specific, which is exactly what the partial unique index on (canonical_name, food_state) WHERE published needs: 7,793 SR Legacy descriptions stay distinct without any invented disambiguator. Curated entries keep their hand-authored canonicalName.
sweepNamingPolicy.displayName: The USDA description verbatim. USDA already writes sentence case ("Mushrooms, white, raw"), which matches the curated entries' own displayName convention, so re-casing it would lose fidelity and risk mangling abbreviations. Distinct display names also keep the search ordering contract (ts_rank DESC, display_name ASC, source_key ASC) deterministic.
sweepNamingPolicy.sourceVersion: "<usdaDataType> <publicationDate as YYYY-MM>", reproducing the reviewed rows' "SR Legacy 2019-04" and "Survey (FNDDS) 2024-10". publicationDate is M/D/YYYY on a detail record and ISO on a list record, so both forms are parsed.
sweepNamingPolicy.sourceCacheKey: "/food/<fdcId>?format=full" - the canonical detail path, which is the key the reviewed rows carry, whether the record was fetched singly or in a POST /foods batch.
sweepNamingPolicy.identityCollisionWithCuratedEntries: A sweep skips any record whose normalised (canonical_name, food_state) matches a curated entry's, on top of skipFdcIdsPresentInFoods, counted under skippedCuratedIdentity. dedupeIdentity's survivor tiebreak is the lexicographically smaller source_key and knows nothing about curation, so without this skip a swept record could unseat a curated identity that search-benchmark.v1.json pins by sourceKey. Swept-versus-swept collisions are left to dedupeIdentity as designed.

sweepPortionPolicy.householdUnitsAreNotWeights: A portion row records the household measure the source states - description, amount and unit - and the gram weight separately. Substituting the gram weight into amount and unit destroys the unit family grocery display depends on ("1 cup, halves" is not "152 g") and contradicts the row's own description. amount and unit come from the portion label; gram_weight comes from gramWeight.
sweepPortionPolicy.unitVocabulary: A unit token is kept when src/utils/units.ts recognises it. A household noun it does not recognise (apple, patty, fillet, pita, sprig, stalk) becomes unit 'each' - the count family, which is what formatCount and pluralizeCount consume - and the noun stays in description, where it is what the user reads.
sweepPortionPolicy.sweptRecordSelection: A swept record has no curated selector, so portions are taken from the record's own foodPortions: entries with gramWeight > 0 and a parseable household label, ordered by sequenceNumber then gramWeight then id, deduplicated by description, at most three. A label of "Quantity not specified" carries no measure and is skipped.

basisPortion.reason: Every published record states its nutrition per 100 g, so a 100 g portion is the source's own basis restated, not an invented weight. It is written for every published food and is the default only when the record states no household portion at all - which is what lets a Foundation record with no foodPortions publish without fabricating a household measure. A household portion always wins the default when one exists.

curatedSafetyContract: Every foods[] entry carries reviewedSafety, and it is the ONLY source of a curated food's allergen_status, allergen_tags and diet_tags. The importer never derives them for a curated entry and never substitutes an empty set: an empty allergenTags list means 'reviewed, and this food contains none of the nine', which is a safety claim, so it is only ever written from a reviewedSafety block whose allergenStatus is 'known'. An entry with no reviewed determination carries allergenStatus 'unknown' and is therefore searchable but never planned as an ingredient (AAP 0.7.3 requires allergen_status = 'known' for every planned ingredient). These values were recovered from the reviewed release at backend 189d348 and are the reviewed determinations themselves, not a re-derivation of them.
